handoff_instructions.purpose: Handoffs document the current state and scope of the project so a new LLM session can pick up exactly where the last one left off. They are the primary continuity mechanism for this project.
what_to_include: A summary of what was done, discussed, decided, or built in this session
What worked and what did not work
Current pipeline state — what scripts exist, what their status is, what the next steps are
A condensed recap of prior sessions so the new LLM has full project context without reading every previous handoff
Open questions or blockers that carry into the next session
what_not_to_include: Exhaustive code listings — reference file paths instead
Decisions that were reversed or abandoned mid-session — only document final state
Speculation about distant future work — stay close to what is actually next
format_rules: This handoff_instructions block must appear at the top of every future handoff
When a user says 'create a handoff for this session,' use this block as the template and fill in the session-specific fields
Prior session summaries should be condensed — one paragraph per session, not a full retelling
Be brief but complete. A new LLM should be able to start working immediately after reading this file

m3_scope.goal: Inference prototype — given a single plan sheet image, produce a line-item budget estimate with total and confidence band.
m3_scope.system_b_inputs: Plan sheet image (or key metrics extracted from it: lot_count, road_LF, job_type, ROW_SF, stripping_depth).
m3_scope.system_b_outputs: Line items (description, qty, unit, unit_price, ext_price), total, confidence band (target: within 10-15% of actual), provenance notes.
m3_scope.approach: 1. Extract metrics from plan sheet via Gemini vision. 2. Analog retrieval — find 2-3 closest historical jobs by lot_count + road_LF. 3. Gap-fill measurable items using knowledge_pack unit_price_distributions. 4. Compute LS items using Type 2 formulas (stripping CY, subgrade SY). 5. Apply derivation rules (sewer/water services = lot_count). 6. Sum to total with confidence band.
m3_scope.analog_retrieval_note: Non-inferable LS items (clear trees, rock allowances, site-specific work) should use analog retrieval cost scaled by lot_count or road_LF ratio — NOT formula.
m3_scope.validation_target: Run against Woodman or another known job as holdout. Compare estimated total to actual $612,676.

open_questions_for_m3: What plan sheet format does Terra Underground receive? Single PDF page, multi-page set, or DWG? M3 input format determines extraction approach.
Drywells rule is broken (0/10 on lot_count). Need a replacement rule — road_LF is the best correlate. Is there a design standard (e.g., 1 drywell per X LF of road)?
6th Ave and Boyds Landing have no confirmed job location — are they in Kootenai/Bonner/Spokane counties? Affects market_context applicability.
Mountainside has road_subgrade_SY=1889 but road_paving_SY=3659 — subgrade is less than paving, which is unusual. Is the subgrade SY labeled 'BOTTOM OF BALLAST' or is some subgrade already existing?
How should M3 handle jobs with LOT GRADING earthwork (separate from ROW earthwork)? Some jobs have significant lot grading costs not tied to road metrics.
